title: Slow-start Mitigator and KV Priming Conductor for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Dedicated tenants occasionally experience degraded tail latency and request rejections during cold attach events when reserved capacity scales up or a new replica handles traffic. Cold start cost and unpredictable throughput undermine SLA guarantees.

Goal: Implement a coordinated, tenant-aware 'Slow-start Mitigator' that reduces cold-start latency and stabilizes throughput by combining streaming weight on-boarding, targeted KV-cache priming, and a lightweight admission controller that enforces throughput guarantees during warm transitions. The feature should be compatible with Dedicated autoscaling policies and integrate with the existing warm pool.

High-level approach: 1) Weight Fast-Stream: stream critical parameter slices in prioritized order (embedding layers, attention/kv-facing layers first) so initial inference can start with partial weights and progressive fidelity. 2) KV Priming Conductor: generate small, deterministic synthetic prefix replays to populate KV caches for common generation patterns and tenant-specific hot prefixes. Priming is tenant-rate limited and fingerprinted to avoid over-priming. 3) Slow-start Admission Controller: when a replica enters service, apply a short ramp window (configurable: default 30s) where throughput is gradually increased using 'throughput tokens' allocated from the tenant's reservation; excess requests fall back to standby replicas or cheaper model variants. 4) Observability + Rollback: expose per-tenant warm metrics and automated fallback if p95 or error-rate degrades beyond thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: New slow-start mitigator can be toggled per-tenant via Dedicated config
Cold-start p95 for first request after attach reduced by >= 25% on synthetic trace tests
KV priming does not exceed configured bandwidth quota and respects tenant isolation
Canary rollout to 5% of fleets with automatic rollback on error-rate > 0.5% above baseline
End-to-end integration tests for weight streaming + priming run in CI with deterministic seed
technical_notes: Weight Fast-Stream will reuse existing streaming protocol but adds slice priority headers and checksum-verified progressive commit
KV priming uses a two-phase fingerprint: (tenant_id, model_id, prefix_hash) to avoid cross-tenant cache poisoning
Admission Controller exposes a backpressure token bucket tied to the Dedicated reservation API and accounts for burst credits
Priming jobs must be scheduled on spare compute to avoid interfering with live inference; use low-priority preemptible slots in fleet

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Priming traffic could steal GPU bandwidth from live inference. Mitigation: enforce strict priming QoS, preemptible nodes, cap priming bandwidth per-region.

Risk: Priming synthetic prefixes may deviate from real workload patterns and give false confidence. Mitigation: seed priming candidates from real request logs and allow customers to supply canonical prefixes.

Risk: Partial-weight inference might yield lower-quality outputs. Mitigation: mark replicas and responses as 'reduced-fidelity' for telemetry and only enable for latency-sensitive paths; provide automatic rollback if quality regressions detected.
